findings.title: Backdating a cut commits the same confirmed transition twice and submits a 10 ms successor fragment
findings.violated_contract: #264 R2 and #211 R1/R8: one-time boundary commit, preserve successor onset, and no burst of stale cuts. Useful early progress must not create unnecessary destructive recognition requests.
findings.reachable_path: For one confirmed A→B transition, an earlier B-active but not-yet-clear frame permits backtracking the actuation coordinate before boundary.normalized_sample. _submit advances submitted_cursor only to that earlier coordinate. Recursive _cut_available sees the same transition's later nominal coordinate as still unsubmitted; backtracking now reaches start/cursor, so the fallback selects the nominal coordinate and submits the intervening fragment as another speaker cut. There is no committed transition identity fencing this second actuation.
decisive_original_evidence: Executed the frozen attribution/evidence/batch Git objects with one transition ID nemotron:11:7:1760: A clear through 1600; B-active probability 0.7 over 1600–1760; two distinct clear B frames thereafter. Before natural seal, the single transition submitted [0,1600] and [1600,1760]. Natural completion then submitted [1760,2400]. Probe exited 0; inner native execution was controlled, with no inference.

Original actual trace build/issue264-validation-first-04/trace.json pins 8c01. At 138463.6091985 the first request ends at 49728; at 138463.6098947 another speaker request submits precisely [49728,49888], 160 samples. Evidence shows B-active probability 0.7632228 over 49728–49888, followed by clear B over 49888–50048 and 50048–50208. Both batch log entries use the same evidence-ready time 138463.5509268.
The second actual transfer repeats the mechanism: cut at 75968, then a separate [75968,76128] 160-sample request. The earlier frame has returning-A probability 0.7360674, followed by clear A frames.

These two actual 0.01-second requests report decode_failure, restart_only recovery, and failed GpuASRDecodeDropped native results. This connects the failure to the observed duplicate-actuation path rather than inferring a cause from request counts.
defenses_and_limits: The first earlier cut is supported onset preservation, not itself the defect; the second application of the same transition is the defect.

Normal two-distinct-frame positive progress remains necessary. A universal minimum duration, dropping short corrections, suppressing every early boundary, or padding every short request would not repair this ownership error.
No GPU failure was rerun. The original actual run supplies native failure evidence; my new reproduction isolates the frozen selector mechanism.

findings.title: Two mapping pieces of one native probability frame are counted as temporal corroboration
findings.violated_contract: #264 R2: confirmation requires distinct temporal evidence; duplicating the same model observation must not create confirmation. Architecture currently promises two distinct clear successor frames.
findings.reachable_path: SpeakerRuntime._mapped preserves capture-block boundaries, so one native 160-sample frame can map to two contiguous source-map pieces. observe creates a separate SpeakerFrame for each piece without retaining their common native-frame identity. transitions increments confirmations for both pieces, qualifying a lone successor impulse.
decisive_original_evidence: Original isolated probe: predecessor A [0,160]; one native B ProbabilityFrame [160,320] mapped as [160,240] plus [240,320]. The accepted view contained three pieces and emitted boundary 160. The same native B frame with one mapping piece emitted no boundary.

A controlled production CausalBatchSession/LocalQwen adapter probe then showed the split single frame actually causes submission of a 160-sample prefix before natural completion; decoded PCM partition was [160,320]. A separate legitimate two-distinct-successor-frame control also progressed.

The actual original trace independently demonstrates real native frames crossing capture-piece boundaries, for example native frame 48320–48480 maps to capture 50048–50176 and 50176–50208. Thus multi-piece native frames are not an invented input shape.
defenses_and_limits: Existing duplicate-delivery tests correctly reject repeated identical evidence, but do not cover two source pieces belonging to one native observation.
The actual two 10 ms decode failures are explained by F1; I do not claim F2 caused those particular failures.
No acoustic incidence or false-boundary rate is claimed. This is a deterministic confirmation-policy violation.

findings.title: Late palette-overflow assignments never reach the readable card
findings.violated_contract: #264 R3 and preserved #211 R5: fifth-and-later keys remain established and distinct even though gray; preserve overflow-divider eligibility and returning-speaker append behavior without moving an already readable card.
findings.reachable_path: After four keys consume the palette, a fifth source first reads unresolved gray. The allocator later settles its correct key with palette_overflow=True and palette_index=None. The presenter requires a non-None palette index to copy the late assignment, so the card retains its unresolved attribution and gray reason instead of its established overflow identity.
decisive_original_evidence: Original six-source controlled presenter probe exited 0. Sources 1–4 established the palette before display. Sources 5 and 6 were displayed unresolved and then received eligible proof at +0.1 seconds.
For source 5, authority key was 4 and authority_overflow was true, while entry_key remained null and gray_reason remained unavailable. Source 6 similarly had authority key 5 but entry_key null.
The final visible pair contained translation 5 and translation 6, both gray, with speaker_divider=false despite distinct established same-epoch overflow keys.
defenses_and_limits: Remaining gray is correct; allocating a fifth color would be wrong. The defect is losing the established identity/overflow disposition at the card.
The same stale card attribution also prevents _compatible_source_card from recognizing a later known returning occurrence; this consequence follows statically from its key comparison.
Text remained readable and unchanged. No actual renderer launch was needed to establish the incorrect authoritative snapshot state.

findings.title: The shared view rejects every intentionally omitted-silence record emitted by the existing producer
findings.violated_contract: #264 R1/R2 and preserved #211 R6: distinguish positively eligible omitted quiet from missing/unprocessed speech; conservative missing-coverage behavior must not discard valid quiet provenance and unnecessarily prevent supported attribution.
findings.reachable_path: The omitted_silence branch selects unobserved source pieces, but then applies the original-audio compact-length equality requirement. SpeakerRuntime._unobserved intentionally encodes omitted capture silence with compact coordinates (0,0), since it was not submitted to the compact diarizer stream. Every nonempty omitted capture range therefore fails line 157. A lawful source footprint intersecting such quiet remains permanently unavailable, and transitions cannot bridge that explicitly accounted quiet.
decisive_original_evidence: Original pure producer/consumer probe used SpeakerRuntime._retain_onset and its normal 8000-sample onset ring, without starting a backend. Ring pressure emitted one omitted_silence record for capture [16000,17600] with compact [0,0].
SpeakerEvidenceView accepted zero new pieces from that real producer record. With clear A over [0,16000], attribution of [0,16000] was identified, but attribution of [0,17600] remained unavailable.

This is reachable when a retained ASR source includes trailing quiet beyond the speaker work horizon, such as a configured VAD/delivery hangover longer than the diarizer's retained tail/ring interval. VAD emits SpeechChunk during active trailing silence (gating.py:317-323), and the capture ledger appends those ranges (ownership.py:317-320).
defenses_and_limits: Do not relax coverage checks for missing speech or fabricate silence. The existing producer's explicit omitted_silence provenance is the positive eligibility distinction.
This probe controlled speech probabilities and exercised the production omission producer; it did not perform acoustic qualification.
The initial omitted ranges visible in the recorded ABA trace precede that request's supplied context start. I do not attribute that run's A/B gray result to this finding.

findings.title: A settled-but-not-yet-applied assignment can color a card after its one-second presentation deadline
findings.violated_contract: #264 R3: the bounded exception is an update within first-readable +1.000 seconds, and the unresolved card must remain gray after that deadline. Evidence settlement and logical snapshot application are separate decisions.
findings.reachable_path: assignment_for/refresh can settle a source before the watcher applies its snapshot. Subsequent refresh skips settled records before checking the deadline, next_deadline no longer includes that record, and the presenter accepts its revision without checking whether the still-gray card's application window has expired. Peer output preparation invokes assignment_for outside the presenter watcher (peer_translation_channel.py:1016).
decisive_original_evidence: Original controlled monotonic-schedule probe: first logical readable gray snapshot at 10.0; eligible proof and assignment_for settlement at 10.9; defer watcher application behind the ownership lock until 11.1. The same card changed gray→gold at logical clock 11.1. The authority retained resolution_delays=[0.9]. Probe exited 0.
The ordinary expiry test covers evidence first processed after the cap, not an assignment already settled before the cap but applied later.
defenses_and_limits: The probe deliberately controlled scheduling/lock availability; it is not a measurement of real GUI or wall-clock frequency.

[INFERENCE] In production this requires watcher scheduling delay across the remaining window. The default bridge replace_snapshot currently performs synchronous mailbox admission rather than a network wait, so I did not establish a normal long bridge-held-lock occurrence.

The source-level missing application guard is conclusive under that schedule. This finding does not concern physical photons or transport latency after an already-applied logical snapshot, and does not justify adding a translation/display hold.
